work_order.understanding: Issue #40 carries four non-blocking findings from the review of #39 (plus a fifth process note with nothing left to change). I checked each against the code on main (13c03ad) and reproduced the load-bearing ones myself. (1) src/domain/opportunities.js:147 — expectedContribution computes Math.trunc(value_micros * pSuccess) - cost_micros and returns 0 when the result is not a safe integer. For a row stored before the micros rename the two money keys are undefined, the arithmetic is NaN, and the guard returns 0 — a value that is also a legitimate break-even contribution, so the sentinel is indistinguishable from an answer. The page already degrades honestly to '—' for exactly these rows; the API does not. (2) Finding 3 is the same lie one layer out: seedOpportunities writes through repositories.opportunities.create, which is INSERT OR IGNORE keyed on the fixed seed id, so a pre-rename row is never rewritten. I reproduced it: seeded a temp DB, overwrote opp_seed_expensive's stored record with the pre-rename shape, and re-ran the seed — it printed 'seed: tenant tenant_demo already present, nothing new written' and exited 0. The recovery #37 promised ('operators re-seed on a fresh DB') therefore does not work, and when every seed row is stale the zero counters make the run report a clean no-op. (3) Finding 4 is a renderer, not a bug in the rename: the local money() at src/web/pages.js:188 bakes in a rupee sign, in a file that already imports and uses the currency-aware formatMoney/fromMicros pair for the dashboard's Qualified CPL at line 355. (4) Finding 2 is a test gap, not a runtime defect: every route-level evaluate assertion checks appended:true, and the false branch is only reachable by calling repositories.evaluations.append directly. I confirmed the route-level test is reachable with no production change — node:test MockTimers on the Date API freezes new Date().toISOString() so two POSTs collide on the (tenant_id, experiment_id, evaluated_at) primary key. (5) The removed if (evaluated.outcome) guard is dropped on purpose: the reviewer judged the removal correct, #39 is merged so there is no PR left to annotate, and the code is not being put back. The root cause shared by 1 and 2 is that the micros rename taught the app to validate micros on the way in and to render '—' on the way out, but never taught it to admit what it does not know: an unreadable row is reported as a number (0) on the wire and as success (nothing written) from the seed, where the honest answer is 'unknown'. This change makes both say unknown.
work_order.root_cause: The micros rename added validation on the write path and honest '—' placeholders on the read path, but left the two places that report on a row the build cannot represent speaking with a confident voice: expectedContribution substituted 0 for an unrepresentable contribution (0 is a legitimate contribution, so the sentinel is indistinguishable from an answer), and seedOpportunities counted only rows it created, so a pre-rename row at a fixed seed id was neither rewritten nor reported. A third renderer hardcodes a currency symbol in the same file that already has the currency-aware one. The fix is to make 'unknown' representable — null on the wire, a thrown error from the seed — instead of overloading a legitimate value with the meaning 'I could not compute this'.
work_order.approach:
Four fixes and one recorded non-fix.

(1) expectedContribution stops lying (src/domain/opportunities.js). It reads value_micros, cost_micros and pSuccess out of the record first and returns null unless all three are usable (both money keys safe integers, pSuccess a finite number), then computes and returns null again if the result is not a safe integer. The guard moves in FRONT of the arithmetic deliberately: Math.trunc(undefined * 0.6) is NaN today, and Math.trunc(null * 0.6) is 0 once the repository starts emitting null (fix 2) — a null that reached the arithmetic would turn 'unknown' into a confident break-even, which is worse than what is being fixed. scoreOpportunity is NOT touched: 0 for a rank key is a last-place ordering, 0 for a displayed amount is a false answer.

(2) The repository stops dropping the two money keys (src/data/repositories.js). shape() projects components with `?? null` for value_micros and cost_micros, so a row this build cannot read comes back as eight components with two explicitly null rather than six keys a caller has to notice are missing. This is a deliberate, stated wire-format change: JSON.stringify drops undefined keys, so today the absent keys are missing entirely and after the change they are present-and-null. That change is observable and is what AC-2 pins. The page's existing `raw == null` guard covers null and undefined alike, so the view is unaffected either way.

(3) The evaluate route's false branch gets a real test (test/api/opportunities.test.js only, no production change). t.mock.timers.enable({apis:['Date']}) plus setTime freezes the route's utcNow() so two back-to-back POSTs land in the same millisecond and the second response is the collision case. setTime takes a number, not a Date. Uses node:test's own MockTimers — stdlib, no new dependency; it prints one ExperimentalWarning and nothing else.

(4) One money renderer in pages.js, currency-aware (src/web/pages.js). money(micros, currency = 'INR') becomes a thin wrapper over the formatMoney/fromMicros pair the file already imports, with two guards that keep the page strictly safer than today: a micros value that is not a safe integer renders '—' instead of today's '₹NaN', and a currency not in ISO_CURRENCIES falls back to INR rather than throwing INVALID_CURRENCY (repositories.tenants.create accepts any string, so an unknown code is a data error, not an exception). The tenant currency is threaded to every renderer that draws money. Two traps: the three Array#map call sites (pages.js:680, :794, :810) pass map's index as the second argument, so each becomes an explicit arrow; and META_CELLS' per-collection cell functions need the currency passed in, which means threading it through metaTable into BOTH of its call sites and through metaRegions into BOTH of its call sites. Scope of the currency fix, stated honestly: it makes the renderer symbol-aware for the four currencies formatMoney knows (INR, USD, EUR, GBP) and code-aware ('JPY 1,000.00') for the rest. It does not make it minor-unit-aware — formatMoney always renders two decimals and never consults MINOR_EXPONENTS. That is a pre-existing property of the repo's canonical formatter, which the dashboard's Qualified CPL already uses, and it is out of scope here (see out_of_scope).

(5) The seed makes an unreadable row loud instead of silent (scripts/seed.js). seedOpportunities already fetches the stored row into `previous` on the line above the write, so the check costs no new query: when a fixed seed id already exists and its stored record has no safe-integer value_micros/cost_micros, throw before create(). The error carries the same {code, message, details} shape as the seed's five existing throws (scripts/seed.js:319, :345, :400, :414, :440) and its message names the real recovery — delete data/app.db and re-seed — because the seed is idempotent by fixed id and can never rewrite a stored record. The seed is NOT atomic and this change does not make it so: seedOpportunities runs last, after the tenant, 13 events, the audit event, the snapshot, 2 learnings, 3 decisions and the derived replay have all committed. Only the opportunity candidates at and after the throwing one are unwritten, and seedExperiments never runs.

Dropped: the removed if (evaluated.outcome) guard (finding 5). Nothing to change and no place left to note it.

alternatives_considered.approach: A backfill migration that rewrites pre-rename records into micros at open time, which is what would truly fix the stale row at the source.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: #37 scoped it out explicitly and it is a larger change than these defects justify: a migration that guesses a currency for rows that never stored one can be wrong in a way that is harder to undo than the null this change makes explicit. The seed's loud throw tells the operator the truth and hands them a one-line recovery, which is the honest state for a demo-tenant database.

alternatives_considered.approach: Omit expected_contribution_micros from the response entirely when the stored components lack the money keys, the second option the reviewer offered.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: A missing key is indistinguishable from an older client that predates the field, and it makes the honest case the same invisible shape as the two component keys JSON.stringify already drops. null is the repo's existing signal for 'no value' on this wire — evaluated.z ?? null at src/api/routes.js:487 — and it is visible to a caller that is looking.

alternatives_considered.approach: Leave expectedContribution's 0 and instead have the route check the components and null the field at src/api/routes.js:367.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It fixes one call site and leaves the domain function still returning a lie to the next caller. The one caller today is the route, but the lie lives in the wrong layer: a pure function asked for a contribution should not invent one.

alternatives_considered.approach: For finding 2, add a clock parameter to buildApp and thread it into the evaluate route so a test can pin evaluated_at.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It is a production seam added for one test, in a codebase whose convention is that the domain stays free of test scaffolding. node:test's own MockTimers on the Date API does the job with zero production change — the test ran against the real app and produced appended:false, duplicate:true with one stored row.

alternatives_considered.approach: For finding 2, let the test call the route's handler function directly instead of going over HTTP.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The finding is precisely that the HTTP path is what is untested; calling the handler directly reproduces the same gap under a different name.

alternatives_considered.approach: For finding 4, fix only the two opportunity money components, as the finding's Fix paragraph describes, and leave money() as the rupee-only helper for the Meta tables and the experiment caps.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: That leaves two renderers of the same concept in one file — the state the finding names as the underlying problem — and fixes a currency bug in two of the four fields that render money. The threaded fix is a handful of extra arguments on functions whose tenant is already in scope.

alternatives_considered.approach: For finding 4, keep money()'s current implementation and only interpolate the symbol from the tenant's currency code.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It leaves a second formatter (toFixed, floats) in the file rather than reusing the integer-only one the repo wrote for exactly this. formatMoney also groups thousands, which is the formatting the dashboard already shows and which the old helper never did.

alternatives_considered.approach: For finding 3, have the seed report the unreadable rows in its result object and a warning line instead of throwing.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The seed's own convention is to fail loudly — it already throws for an invalid candidate, event, decision, learning and experiment (scripts/seed.js:319, :345, :400, :414, :440). A warning on stdout is what the current silent counter is, one line louder; the throw is what stops an operator believing a clean no-op.

alternatives_considered.approach: Make the seed transactional so the throw really does leave nothing behind, and keep the first draft's stronger test assertion.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Wrapping the whole seed in a transaction is a larger change than this issue justifies and would alter behaviour for every other seed failure too. The honest, cheap thing is to assert what the code actually does: the opportunity phase is last, so a stale-row throw leaves the tenant/events/learnings/decisions/snapshot committed and writes no candidate. The test says that, so nobody later reads a passing test as a promise of atomicity.

alternatives_considered.approach: Give AC-5 a browser step by POSTing a USD spend event to auto-create a USD tenant (the critique's proposed fix) and loading the page.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: I checked and this does not work. src/api/routes.js:158 does auto-create a tenant from a spend event's currency, so the first draft's reason ('the only tenant the seed creates is INR') was not a reachability argument and is corrected here — but tenants.list() is ORDER BY created_at, id (src/data/repositories.js:27) and firstTenant() renders [0], so a USD tenant created after the demo tenant is not the one the page draws. Seeding a USD-first database would be reachable, and is out of scope. AC-5 stays test-verified with the real reason recorded.

alternatives_considered.approach: Extend formatMoney to consult MINOR_EXPONENTS so zero-decimal (JPY, KRW) and three-decimal (KWD, BHD) currencies render the right amount, as the critique's second option suggests.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Correct as a fact, wrong as a change here. formatMoney's two-decimal output and its four-symbol table are pre-existing properties of the repo's canonical formatter, which the dashboard's Qualified CPL already renders through at src/web/pages.js:355 — this change neither introduces them nor widens them, and for JPY the output goes from '₹1000.00' to 'JPY 1,000.00', which is a currency label corrected and an amount scale left exactly as it was. Rewriting minor-unit handling in money.js is a money-module change unrelated to the four findings in this issue. Recorded in out_of_scope and residual_risks rather than done quietly.

assumptions: node:test MockTimers with {apis:['Date']} freezes new Date() for the whole process while enabled, and t.mock.timers.reset() restores it per test. setTime takes a number, not a Date (a Date throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE on Node 22.23.2). Verified by running the exact test shape against the real app on this runner, not assumed.

The Meta adapter guarantees integer micros for daily_budget_micros and spend_micros: src/integrations/meta_ads/index.js:139 and :152 validate both with isCount. The lastGood() snapshot is a hardcoded integer-micros fixture set in src/integrations/meta_ads/fake.js:54-63 with no persistence layer, so no code path can write a non-integer into a snapshot row. The new money()'s safe-integer guard is the belt-and-braces on top of that.

repositories.tenants.create accepts any currency string and does not validate it against ISO_CURRENCIES, so an unknown code is reachable in the data. The new money() falls back to INR for it. The pre-existing inline formatMoney call on the Qualified CPL (pages.js:355) has the same exposure and is fixed as a side effect of routing it through money().

Nothing outside src/web/pages.js, src/api/routes.js and the tests reads row.components or the opportunity money fields. Checked expectedContribution, money(, opportunityRow, experimentCard, metaTable, metaRegions, rankedList, firstTenant and data-component across the repo; every call site is enumerated in files[] with its line number.
scripts/seed.js's seedOpportunities is the only writer of seed opportunities; nothing else creates a row at a fixed seed id, so the stale-shape check cannot be tripped by a legitimate write path.

The pages tests' fixtures use an INR tenant, so the formatting change is grouping-only for the existing assertions. Checked every rupee assertion in test/: only :228, :431 and :432 change; :119, :145, :192, :227, :474, :478 and :480 already match what formatMoney produces.
No new runtime dependency: the clock-frozen test uses node:test's built-in MockTimers, and the currency work uses the formatMoney/fromMicros pair already imported by the file.
unknowns: Whether the reviewer would rather the stale-row check live in openDatabase as a startup warning than in the seed. The seed is where the operator looks and where the wrong promise was made, so that is where it is; a startup check would catch a stale row for someone who never runs the seed.

Whether a stored record whose money keys are present but whose stored value differs from today's seed data should also throw. Scoped to the unreadable shape only, as the finding describes. A value drift is a different problem — the seed is idempotent by fixed id, so a changed seed value silently does not apply — but throwing on it would break repeat runs the moment anyone edits a seed figure.

Whether absent-key and explicit-null are meant to be distinguishable to API clients. This change makes them distinguishable, deliberately, and AC-2 says so. If no client cares, dropping the shape() projection would be a two-token simplification — but it would leave GET returning six keys for a row whose POST response says null, which is the inconsistency worth avoiding.

The operator-facing recovery instruction currently lives only in #37's PR description, which this change cannot edit. The error message is therefore the durable home for it; no document in the repo mentions re-seeding, so a runbook change had no home to go in.
risks: Routing every money render through formatMoney changes user-visible output by adding thousands grouping (₹6000.00 becomes ₹6,000.00, ₹4000.00 becomes ₹4,000.00). Three existing assertions encode the old shape and are updated by this change at test/web/pages.test.js:228, :431 and :432; any downstream reader or screenshot that quoted the old string sees the new one. This is deliberate — it is the formatting the reviewer's own fix text asked for and the dashboard already showed — but it is a visible change, not a pure refactor.

The seed now fails on a database it previously reported as seeded, so its exit code goes from 0 to non-zero. Anything invoking `npm run sdlc:seed` in CI or a dev script will start failing on such a database. That is the intent, and the error message is the only guidance the operator gets.

The shape() change is a wire-format change: the two money keys move from absent to explicit-null on rows this build cannot read. Consumers distinguishing the two see the difference. Stated in AC-2 and in the code comment rather than left as a surprise.

MockTimers is an experimental node:test API and prints an ExperimentalWarning during the test run. It is stdlib and test-only; if the project would rather not carry an experimental API in CI, the alternative is the buildApp clock parameter, which is a larger production change.

money() now depends on ISO_CURRENCIES being a complete list for the fallback to be right. A tenant on a valid-but-unlisted currency renders as its bare code ('JPY 1,000.00') rather than a symbol, and a tenant on a completely unknown code falls back to INR — never a crash, but never right either for ~176 of the ~180 codes.
out_of_scope: A backfill migration for pre-rename records. #37 scoped it out and it needs a currency the record never stored; this issue makes the stale state loud and the wire honest instead.

Restoring the if (evaluated.outcome) guard removed in #39 (finding 5). The reviewer judged the removal correct, the guard was dead, and #39 is merged — there is no PR description left to annotate and no defect to fix.
Splitting the removed guard into its own commit. Same finding, same reason: the change it refers to is already merged.

Minor-unit-exponent rendering in formatMoney. money.js:89 defines MINOR_EXPONENTS and allocate() uses it, but formatMoney always renders two decimals, so a zero-decimal (JPY, KRW, VND, ISK, UGX, CLP) or three-decimal (BHD, JOD, KWD, OMR, TND, IQD, LYD) tenant renders an amount scaled wrong. This is a pre-existing property of the repo's canonical formatter, reachable today through the dashboard's Qualified CPL, and it is not made worse or better by routing the other renderers through it. Fixing it is a money-module change unrelated to the four findings in this issue.

Symbols for the ~176 ISO codes formatMoney does not have a glyph for. The renderer becomes code-aware for them ('JPY 1,000.00') rather than symbol-aware, and says the currency honestly instead of claiming to be rupee. A symbol table is a money-module concern.

A browser-reachable non-INR tenant. AC-5 is test-verified because firstTenant() renders tenants.list()[0] under a deterministic ORDER BY created_at, id; seeding a USD-first demo database would make it browser-reachable and is a seed-data decision, not a fix for this issue.

Pinning the tenants.list() ordering in a test. The ordering is what makes AC-5 test-only, so a future change to it would silently invalidate the reasoning — but no existing test depends on it and adding one is a separate concern.

The pre-existing single-currency assumption in the Meta tables and experiment caps as a product decision. This change makes all of them currency-aware; it does not decide whether v1 should be single-currency, which is a product call with no evidence either way in the repo.
Comparing stored seed values against current seed data. Throwing on drift would break legitimate repeat runs after any seed edit.
Making the seed transactional. A stale-row throw leaves the earlier seed phases committed; wrapping the seed in a transaction would change behaviour for every other seed failure too.
residual_risks: A stale row still exists after this change. It is now reported as unknown (null money components, null contribution, '—' on the page) and the seed refuses to report success over it, but nothing repairs it. The operator's job is to delete the database and re-seed. A clean seed exit is now the signal that the database is readable by this build — which is the qa_script's first step, and should stay first.

The seed is loud but not atomic. Because seedOpportunities runs last, a stale-row throw leaves the tenant, 13 events, the audit event, the snapshot, 2 learnings, 3 decisions and the derived replay committed, and never reaches seedExperiments. Anyone reading a passing test/ops/seed.test.js as a promise of atomicity would be wrong; the test says so in a case name.

The evaluate route's duplicate:false path is covered by a clock-frozen test, not one that exercises the real clock. The production code path is identical either way — the route stamps utcNow() — but the coverage depends on MockTimers behaving as it does today.

The currency fix is verified for USD by test only, and only on a renderPage path. It is symbol-aware for the four currencies formatMoney knows and code-aware for the rest, and it is minor-unit-blind for all of them (see out_of_scope). AC-4's browser step proves the INR rendering and the shared formatter, not the multi-currency behaviour itself.

A record written by a build that predates the micros rename is indistinguishable on the wire from a record deliberately written with unknown money. Both are null. That is the intended reading, but the API cannot tell you which build wrote a row.

A page that throws in money() would take down the whole dashboard rather than one cell. The safe-integer and known-currency guards exist for exactly that, and AC-7 covers them — but they are guards in a renderer, not a type system, and a new money() call site added later without them would be unguarded.
work_order.confidence_rationale: The root cause is verified by execution, not by reading: I reproduced the 0-on-the-wire contribution, the dropped component keys, the seed's silent exit-0 no-op over a planted pre-rename row (running the exact plant-and-reseed sequence that is now in the qa_script), and the route-level duplicate over HTTP with MockTimers. Every call site of every symbol this change touches is now enumerated with a line number after re-checking them myself, and the critique's two real undercounts — metaRegions' two callers and the three Array#map sites — are corrected rather than asserted away. What keeps this off the high 80s: three judgement calls remain genuinely open and are recorded as unknowns rather than resolved — whether the stale-row check belongs in the seed or in openDatabase, whether the shape() null projection belongs in this issue at all, and whether absent-key versus explicit-null is meant to be visible to clients. None is load-bearing: drop the projection and fix (1) still holds, move the check to startup and the operator still learns the truth. Two things I could not fully verify: whether the page can ever see a non-integer from a provider path (the only provider is a hardcoded fake, so I believe not, but I did not prove the live provider shares that shape), and whether the grouping change in the three test assertions breaks anything outside the repo.
work_order.debate_summary: The critique was right about the diagnosis and right about the plan not being executable as written; it was wrong about three things and overreaching on one. Its two blocking findings stand and I fixed both. The qa_script pointed at a node one-liner in residual_risks that does not exist — I confirmed by reading the section and then wrote and ran a replacement that plants a pre-rename row and reproduces the current silent exit-0, so that verification step is now real rather than referenced. The seed test case asserted 'the seed fails before writing anything', which is false: seedOpportunities runs after the tenant, events, learnings, decisions and snapshot have all committed. I narrowed the assertion to what is true and named the non-atomic boundary. Its evidence slightly overstated this — it said earlier candidates are already written before a later one throws, but the planted row opp_seed_expensive is the FIRST candidate, so no candidate is written at all; the false part is specifically the earlier phases. I kept its recommended option (narrow the assertion) and rejected its alternative (reorder or make the seed abort before writing), which is a larger change than this issue justifies. Its three caller-counting findings were correct: metaRegions has two call sites (:293 partial, :313 ideal), metaTable has two (:242 ideal, :251 the last-good error path), and there are three Array#map sites (:680, :794, :810) where map's index would land in a new currency parameter. I folded all of them in with line numbers, and the :251 path is the one that matters most for a currency bug since it is exactly where a wrong symbol would render. Its AC-2 finding was right and I rewrote the criterion: the curl already returns 8 today and is already asserted at test/api/opportunities.test.js:88, so it cannot distinguish fixed from broken code. Its finding that the money() fix is symbol-aware for 4 of ~180 codes and minor-unit-blind for all of them is factually correct — I read money.js:89 and :132-134 to confirm — but I did not adopt its fix. The two-decimal output and four-symbol table are pre-existing properties of the repo's canonical formatter, which the dashboard's Qualified CPL already renders through, so this change neither introduces nor worsens them; for JPY the output goes from a false '₹1000.00' to an honest 'JPY 1,000.00' with the same amount scale. I recorded the limit in AC-5, in risks, and in out_of_scope rather than widening a bug-fix ticket into a money-module rewrite. Its wire-format finding is right that the change is observable and under-specified, so I stated it explicitly in AC-2 and in the code comment; I rejected its recommendation to drop fix (2) entirely, because leaving GET returning six keys for a row whose POST response carries a null contribution is the exact inconsistency this issue exists to remove. Its AC-5 finding had a correct premise and a wrong fix. The premise: the first draft's stated reason ('the only tenant the seed creates is INR') is not a reachability argument, and src/api/routes.js:158 does auto-create a tenant from a spend event's currency — I verified that. The fix: POSTing a USD spend event and loading the page would not show a USD tenant, because tenants.list() is ORDER BY created_at, id (src/data/repositories.js:27) and firstTenant() renders [0], so a tenant created after the demo one is not drawn. I kept AC-5 test-verified and recorded the real reason. I dismissed two of its claims outright. The missed-edge-case item saying test/domain/opportunities.test.js:84 'is not in files[] at all, so that test would be left asserting the old behaviour and would fail' misreads the schema — files[] is for source and tests[] is for tests, and that file is already in tests[] with action 'edit'. Its substance is real, so rather than dismiss it silently I moved the exact three assertions to invert into the tests[] case text where an implementer will see them. The regression risk that a lastGood() snapshot row carrying non-integer money would throw INVALID_MONEY and 500 the dashboard is unfounded for this codebase: the only provider is FakeMetaAdsProvider, whose lastGood() returns a hardcoded integer-micros fixture set with no persistence layer, and the new money()'s safe-integer guard would degrade such a row to '—' rather than throw regardless. I also corrected the proposal's own 'the other four seed throws', which lists five: scripts/seed.js:319, :345, :400, :414, :440.
